newsitem.title: PERU: Peru tightens security in jails with MRTA rebels.
newsitem.headline: Peru tightens security in jails with MRTA rebels.

text.p: Peru has tightened prison security and isolated jailed Tupac Amaru rebels following the death of 14 of their comrades in a government raid that freed 71 hostages, prison sources said on Thursday.

"They are well controlled so that news of the (hostage rescue) does not provoke riots. At the moment they cannot leave the cells at all and there are no visits," a police officer at a maximum security jail in northern Peru said.

Peruvian security forces on Tuesday assaulted the Japanese Ambassador's residence where the hostages were held by the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA). The raid ended the 18-week crisis and left all the rebels dead.
A nun, who works with prisoners accused of belonging to the MRTA, complained authorities had stopped her jail visits after Tuesday's assault.
"There are many we believe to be innocent. But now they are suffering this tough treatment because they are regarded as MRTA members," the nun, who asked to remain anonymous, said.
The MRTA has said it feared authorities would deliberatley provoke prison riots to give them an excuse to kill their comrades.

The group also expects jailed members to immediately suffer physical and psychological torture after the MRTA failed in its bid to force the government to free 450 rebels with its takover of the diplomatic residence.
The hostage crisis ended Tuesday when commandos stormed the building as rebels played a mini-soccer game. One hostage and two officers died in the attack.
